html:
The Hixkaryana are an Indigenous people of the Nhamundá River, a northern tributary of the Amazon in Brazil. About 600 people speak their language, which belongs to the Cariban family, like that of the Trio to the north.

The language is famous among linguists. In the 1970s Desmond Derbyshire showed that its basic word order is object, verb, subject, a pattern once thought not to exist in any human language. The Hixkaryana live by farming, fishing and hunting, and their villages took in people from other small groups of the region over the 1900s. See also the wider Amazon peoples.
